articles.socialMediaShareDescription: Pre-Orders are Open for Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis!

content.value: The wait is over. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis arrives February 12, 2027, on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Steam, and Nintendo Switch 2. Check out the State of Play trailer below for your first look at new gameplay.

fields.contentfulName: Legacy of Atlantis Release Date Trailer
fields.html: <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/fn1EREGsdFg?si=38WU0bRz6GJnurH6" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>

content.value: Built on Unreal Engine 5 by Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog, Legacy of Atlantis pairs stunning visuals with modern design sensibilities and unexpected new twists, all while staying true to the tone and atmosphere that defined Lara's original journey.

Environments have grown in scope and scale, making exploration, combat, and puzzle-solving feel entirely reimagined. In Peru's Lost Valley, puzzles have been redesigned from scratch. Spaces that once stood alone now flow into interconnected environments, giving players multiple angles of approach and new paths to discover.

Fan-favorite moments like the cog puzzle return in completely reimagined form. These reinventions bring Peru fully to life, layering in personality and history that make every iconic moment land harder than ever.
Whether you've been raiding tombs since '96 or this is your first adventure with Lara Croft, this is the definitive way to experience where the legend started.
Pre-orders are live now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Steam. Three editions are available: Standard, Deluxe, and Collector's.
Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis (full game digital download)
Lara Croft vs. The T-Rex Statue

Yes, you read that right. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on February 12, 2027. Play on the go, at home, or wherever adventure calls — experience the same cinematic scale and fluid gameplay, designed for Nintendo Switch 2.
Pre-orders for Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis on Nintendo Switch™ 2 will be available at a later date. Stay tuned for more updates.
Digital pre-orders for the Standard and Deluxe Editions are available now on
. Physical editions (including the Collector’s Edition) will be available at select retailers in the coming days.
Secure your copy now and follow the official Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis @PlayTombRaider social channels for the latest updates!

fields.name: Lara Croft and Temple of Osiris

fields.title: Temple of osiris blog header
fields.description: Dramatic Tomb Raider promotional key art featuring four heroes standing together in a battle-ready pose against a dark, smoky, ruins-filled background. At the center is Lara Croft, depicted in her classic look with dark ponytail, teal tank top, brown shorts, and knee pads, dual-wielding pistols with both guns firing. To her left stands a muscular man in a red shirt firing a revolver with a red energy flash. To her right is a warrior dressed in an ancient Egyptian pharaoh's nemes headdress and armor, wielding a large staff. Furthest right is a young woman in Egyptian-style robes raising a glowing blue magical scepter. Looming behind the group is a massive snarling black wolf-like creature with bared fangs, emerging from the darkness. Scorpion claws and twisted dark tree branches frame the edges of the composition, reinforcing the supernatural danger the heroes face.

articles.socialMediaShareDescription: Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris is available now on GameNight!

content.value: Lara Croft has starred in many adventures over the decades, from ancient tombs to shipwrecked islands. While Lara can handle most of her exploits solo, she still needs the occasional helping hand – most notably in
Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris
, where Lara joins with up to three companions for fast-paced top-down action and puzzle solving. With
coming to Game Night, we talked with Ryan Meyer, development lead for the Game Night version, about adapting Lara Croft’s cooperative adventure.
Game Night allows players to instantly jump into a game without dedicated hardware, using their phone as the controller. What makes
Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris
a good fit for the platform?
I've been having a lot of fun with
Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris

because of its co-op/competitive gameplay. It's a great fit for people to sit down on a couch together and play through it. You work together to beat the game, but you can also compete on things like gem count and score charts at the end of each level. It's super quick to get in and out of, and it offers a lot of moment-to-moment gameplay that makes everyone laugh, groan or cheer together.

fields.title: LC2 Screenshot Ball Cage
fields.description: A Tomb Raider game screenshot depicting an intense isometric combat scene set in a circular sandy arena at night. The enclosed battlefield is surrounded by wooden spike fences and tall dark barriers, with torches burning along the perimeter. At the center stands a crumbling ancient stone rotunda structure engulfed in fire and debris. Two player characters are visible — one on the upper left highlighted with a red selection ring aiming a weapon, and one on the upper right with a green ring in a combat stance. A third character near the bottom center is surrounded by a blue magical circle. The arena floor is scattered with glowing teal Zia symbol rings, purple gem pickups, a yellow arc marker, and green energy pools near the central structure. Explosions, fire bursts, smoke clouds, flying debris, and white energy beams fill the chaotic scene, suggesting a major battle or boss encounter in progress.

content.value: was not originally designed for touch screen controls; how did you approach designing the controller interface for Game Night?

This was an interesting challenge because this isn't typical mobile game development. Sure, you're still playing on a mobile device, but you have to consider that the player is not looking at their phone most of the time. So, we needed to make sure the player could easily access every game action intuitively and ergonomically. The first step was mapping every action to a button on the touchscreen, then deciding on the control style and ensuring the buttons were large enough to hit accurately and reliably. Then it came down to playtesting and iteration.
What were the biggest hurdles you faced in designing and implementing the touch controls

When moving to touch control, you really only want to have up to two touch inputs needed at a time. There are several inputs that work well with a gamepad that don't easily translate to touch. For example, to engage the grappling hook you need to move, aim and then hit the trigger. Then you need to hold down the trigger to keep the grappling hook connected. Then when you need to jump with the grappling hook out, that's three inputs at a time. So, we needed to figure out a solution. Do we replace the mobile controller when the grappling hook is out? Do we auto fire the grappling hook? In this case we changed the grappling hook to toggle to release.

fields.title: LC2 Screenshot Puzzle
fields.description: An isometric view of a combat scene inside an ancient Egyptian tomb or temple. The sandy, torchlit environment features stone brick walls, carved pharaoh statues, crumbling columns, and a row of tall metal spikes serving as a barrier across the middle of the scene. Four characters are engaged in battle: one character highlighted with a red danger ring appears to be under attack on the left side of the spikes, while another raises a glowing orb nearby. On the right side, a heavily armored warrior character stands within a teal glowing shield ability circle, and a third enemy holds a red flare. Teal and blue magical energy effects illuminate the ground around the fighters. Wall-mounted torches and small braziers cast warm orange light throughout the dimly lit stone chamber.

content.value: Then there was the inventory. For the original design, players were all meant to share the screen when changing their inventory selections. That meant if one player wanted to swap a weapon or ring it would pause the game for everyone. With the Game Night version, we can take advantage of each player having their own device. We were able to implement a new game flow that allows players to individually adjust their inventory on their mobile device without pausing gameplay. With this change the gameplay continues smoothly and keeps the action going.
Which character is your favorite to play?

Personally I like characters that have the grappling hook, so Lara and Carter. I have to confess that when the whole team is walking across the grappling hook to get to the next platform I've given in to the temptation to pull the grappling hook back. "Whoops! I slipped! I guess somebody should pick up all these gems, don't worry I'll take care of it."

fields.title: LC2 Screenshot Flood Tomb
fields.description: A Tomb Raider game screenshot showing an isometric combat scene set in a darkened, overgrown ancient ruins courtyard at night. The multi-tiered stone environment is covered in vines and moss, lit by scattered torches and glowing blue crystals on the ground. Four characters are engaged in battle across different levels of the ruins: one character ringed in red is fighting a skeleton enemy in the foreground, another with a green selection ring is firing a weapon in the center, a third is conjuring a teal magical energy beam on the upper right, and a yellow glowing ring marks another position nearby. Swirling smoke, ice crystal effects, and magical blue light trails fill the scene. Stone archways, clay pots, crumbling columns, and overgrown walls decorate the atmospheric background, creating a haunted, ancient temple atmosphere.

content.value: Any other stories or thoughts on the development that players would enjoy hearing about?

The web controller went through a lot of iteration. First, we had three buttons on each side of the web controller, each near a virtual thumbstick. We started with an “expedition” theme to the background design. Through playtesting we changed the theme to be “Mystical Egyptian,” which was a better fit for all the characters. We also moved the mine button with every iteration of layout design. Here are some of the work in progress images we went through when approaching the final design:

fields.title: Picture1-740
fields.description: Smartphone mockup displaying a custom touchscreen game controller interface themed around Tomb Raider. The screen features a brown textured background with gold circular control overlays, including a directional pad on the left and a large movement control on the right. Additional icons include a pistol, a flaming torch, and a curved arrow symbol. In the upper-left corner is a portrait of Lara Croft framed by decorative wings.

fields.title: Picture3
fields.description: A steampunk-styled UI panel from a Tomb Raider game featuring an Egyptian pharaoh character portrait at the center, framed in gold with laurel leaves. Surrounding the portrait are eight circular teal-glowing icon buttons arranged symmetrically on a bronze/brown textured background with gold trim. Icons include an ankh, a pistol with rotation arrows (weapon swap), an anchor, a compass/wheel, a lasso/rope tool, a hand gesture, a targeting reticle, and a rectangular layout button. A large golden downward-pointing arrow emblem decorates the center background.

fields.title: Outfit Examples
fields.description: A Tomb Raider promotional image advertising unlockable cosmetic content, with bold white text at the bottom reading "UNLOCK 10 NEW OUTFITS." Ten versions of Lara Croft are displayed in a lineup against a dark textured background, each wearing a distinct costume skin. From left to right the outfits include: a dark navy tactical suit with gold belt, a red racing jacket with goggles and grey pants, a pink and gold fantasy warrior outfit with armor shoulder pads, a sleek grey pilot or spy jumpsuit with blue-tinted glasses, a striking red and gold Asian-inspired royal outfit with a gold crown centerpiece, a sporty crop top and red patterned shorts with orange sunglasses, a black and neon green athletic racing bodysuit with knee pads, a gold and bronze striped fantasy skirt armor set, and a classic tan safari explorer outfit with a white hat. Each Lara model shares the same stylized animated character design but is differentiated by her unique costume, color palette, and accessories.

content.value: Lara’s got a new look… or ten. Try on a whole new wardrobe with enhanced abilities and special upgrades, but first you’ll have to earn them. Unlock the whole collection by completing 30 new challenges. Each outfit is inspired by a location in the games, can you tell which ones?

fields.title: Achievements Mockup
fields.description: A Tomb Raider Challenge Mode promotional image displaying eleven achievement or challenge badge cards arranged in two horizontal rows against a dark background. At the top center is an orange distressed banner reading "Challenge Mode" with a crowned skull icon. Each badge is designed to look like an aged, weathered parchment tile with dark red and magenta illustrated artwork. The badges depict various challenge themes including: a figure holding a compass, Lara Croft seated atop a large pile of skulls, a triumphant silhouette with arms raised in a sunburst, a silhouette standing victorious on a mountain peak, Lara making a peace sign gesture, a shark, a crouching figure with large animal paw prints, a silhouette walking a winding path through trees, Lara in her wetsuit costume beside a no-swimming symbol, a stopwatch with a running figure indicating a speed challenge, and a silhouette figure in an action pose against a pink splattered background. The overall aesthetic is retro adventure poster style rendered in warm brown, pink, and magenta tones.

content.value: Increase your CR (challenge rating) with modifiers in Challenge Mode to replay your favorite levels on a more challenging difficulty. Earn all 15 new achievements as you unlock new outfits. The higher your CR, the bigger the rewards.

fields.title: Combat Screenshot
fields.description: A Tomb Raider game screenshot showing a dramatic action sequence inside an ancient Greco-Roman style stone temple or colosseum. Lara Croft, dressed in her gold and black ancient warrior armor with a red scarf and gold laurel hair accessory, is leaping acrobatically through the air in the upper right of the frame. She is surrounded by two large dinosaur creatures — a towering red-orange theropod dinosaur dominates the left side of the image, lunging forward with its jaws wide open revealing sharp teeth and outstretched clawed arms, while a second large brown dinosaur is partially visible in the foreground right. The ornate interior setting features tall stone columns, decorative carved friezes with laurel wreaths and lion head details, mosaic tiled floors, and warm amber lighting, creating a sense of grand ancient architecture contrasting with the prehistoric danger.

content.value: Do you want a nature walk through the Lost Valley or a hard grind through the Natla’s Mines? Replay any level your way with customizable modifiers for weapons, enemy type, damage, and more. Share the modifiers you recommend for the ultimate level build with #ChallengeMode and connect to the community.

fields.title: New Platforms
fields.description: A Tomb Raider game promotional image showcasing the title running across three different devices, arranged against a dark textured brown background. The largest and central device is an iPad or tablet displayed in portrait-leaning landscape orientation, showing a remastered close-up of Lara Croft in a brown outfit, red scarf, and white safari hat, standing inside an ornate ancient stone temple with decorated ceilings and columns. In the lower left is a smaller tablet or iPhone in landscape orientation displaying an older, more blocky original-graphics version of a Lara Croft character navigating mossy stone ruins, representing the classic retro gameplay. In the lower right is a Nintendo Switch handheld console showing Lara Croft in her green and black futuristic wetsuit costume with tactical goggles, posed in a rocky cavern environment. The three screens together illustrate the game's availability across multiple platforms and its visual range from classic to remastered graphics.

fields.title: Lara Birthday FWH blog header
fields.description: A Tomb Raider 30th anniversary celebratory illustration depicting Lara Croft in a stylized comic book art style, leaning casually on a rocky ledge against a lush misty jungle and floating mountains backdrop. Lara has dark braided hair, wears round red-tinted sunglasses which she is adjusting with one fingerless-gloved hand, a teal tank top, and a tactical backpack harness. She has a warm, confident smile. In front of her sits a detailed miniature diorama birthday cake decorated to resemble a Tomb Raider scene, featuring two red theropod dinosaurs flanking a waterfall and jungle temple on a wooden slice base. Atop the cake are gold metallic number "30" candles with lit flames, celebrating the franchise's 30th anniversary. The overall mood is playful and celebratory while nodding to iconic Tomb Raider imagery including the classic dinosaur encounters.

The shirt's design displays the "Tomb Raider" logo in large distressed crumbling orange stone lettering arranged in two stacked rows. Overlaid on the text is an illustrated figure of Lara Croft in her classic look — teal tank top, white shorts, dark hair flowing — dynamically climbing or scaling upward, reaching high with one arm while holding a rope that trails below her. The illustration style is bold and graphic with a limited color palette of teal, white, red, and orange against the black fabric. The overall design has an energetic, action-packed feel capturing Lara's adventurous spirit.

content.value: Thank you so much for being with us on this journey, and we look forward to many more years of tombs, traps, and celebrations.

is set in the wake of a mythical cataclysm that has unleashed ancient secrets and awakened the mysterious forces that guard them. When the most notorious treasure hunters from around the world descend on the region, Lara races to uncover the truth buried beneath the fractured landscape and stop those who would use its power for their own gain. As the ancient world collides with the present, Lara must decide who to trust among rivals and allies to prevent a catastrophe and protect a secret that could reshape the future.

delivers the largest Tomb Raider world yet where Lara will traverse a landscape full of secrets, delve into lost tombs packed with intricate puzzles, and solve ancient mysteries using her unmatched brilliance and richly customized adventure tech. Perfect for longtime fans and newcomers alike, players will experience an exhilarating story of trust and betrayal that tests Lara Croft in new ways.

The game arrives in 2026 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and Steam.

However, the temple remains guarded, hinting at future dangers.

fields.description: Official key art for Tomb Raider I•II•III Remastered – Challenge Mode. The left half features three stylized versions of Lara Croft in different outfits posed against vertical colored backdrop panels. The center and largest figure wears ornate gold ancient warrior armor with a red scarf and gold laurel hair accessory. To her left, Lara is dressed in a green and black futuristic wetsuit with tactical goggles, holding a scoped assault rifle, set against a teal underwater background. To her right, Lara wears an olive military tactical suit with aviator sunglasses, dual-wielding silver pistols against a dark green background. The right half of the image displays the game's official logo: "Tomb Raider I•II•III Remastered" in large distressed orange stone-textured lettering, with "Challenge Mode" highlighted in an orange banner beneath it, featuring a small skull icon, all set against a dark charcoal textured background.

fields.title: TR1-3Challenge key art zoom
fields.description: Tomb Raider game promotional artwork showcasing three different costume variants or skins of Lara Croft displayed side by side against a dark textured background with three vertical panel backdrops. The center figure is the most prominent, depicted in ornate gold and bronze ancient warrior armor with a red scarf, gold laurel leaf hair accessory, and a braided updo, set against a warm amber temple background. To the left, Lara wears a green and black futuristic wetsuit with tactical goggles pushed up on her head, carrying a scoped assault rifle, set against an underwater teal backdrop. To the right, Lara is styled in a sleek olive/military green tactical outfit with aviator sunglasses and a side braid, dual-wielding silver pistols against a dark green background. All three versions share the same confident, combat-ready expression and stylized animated art style.
